Closed by the strategy after one bar for a small gain; the late entry after a long run limited the upside as noted, and the path says too little to move the grade.
Closed after one bar for a small loss with no favourable move; dead-chop fade with crowded exposure and an oversized stop deserved to be skipped.
Entered after the move was spent and sat for a very long hold with little favourable excursion before the wide stop hit; the late-entry criticism was right.
Fading a quiet grind higher with a very wide stop lost more than 1R; price pushed well through the area the short relied on, consistent with no directional edge.
One-bar strategy close paid about 1R, more than the recorded excursion, so the figure looks cost or fill driven; the false-breakout chop setup was still low quality.
Marginal trend breakout that stalled and stopped out for a standard 1R loss; the tightening trail limited damage as the blind grade expected.
Buying a reclaim inside a strong downtrend should have been rated lower at decision time; ADX and the size of the prior fall were visible, and price went far against the position.
Well-formed trend breakdown that reversed quickly after a modest favourable move; a normal stop-out for a setup with moderate conviction.
Strategy closed after one bar for a small net loss despite a decent favourable move and little heat; the trend pullback thesis was not tested by the bracket.
Break in thin chop was rejected as the last bar suggested, little favourable move, then a full stop loss; the skip verdict stands.
Over 2R of open profit appeared mid-trade and was handed back to a small net loss at strategy close; the unrealistic target and crowding argued for skipping.
Tight stop survived with moderate heat and the nearly 5R target filled within a handful of bars; the sl_too_tight worry did not bite here, but it was a narrow escape.
Thin-volume chop break rose to over 1R in profit and then reversed to a full stop; weak edge and crowded same-way exposure meant the early gain was never reliable.
Conflicted book exposure and a transitional regime produced a short time-exit loss with almost no favourable move; consistent with the late, crowded assessment.
Stale sweep and no fresh displacement; price pushed 1.7R against the very wide stop with almost no favourable move. The wide stop only enlarged the loss; the entry should have been skipped.

Spent pullback at very low confidence; it never gained more than 0.2R and was closed by reconciliation at a small loss. Weak setup confirmed, but the exit was not the bracket so exit quality is unclear.

Chased entry in a strong trend gave up a 7R run and then took a 5R drawdown before stopping out for a modest net loss. Reported stop geometry looks unreliable; a trail or earlier exit would have banked much more.

The 6R target was never reached but price ran past 4R before stopping out; the stop-labelled exit still booked a gain. A nearer target around 4R would have captured the move; the far target was the flaw.
Trend-aligned pullback short with sound bracket; it got 1.2R in favour, then reversed through the stop. A reasonable low-edge trade that lost; nothing in the path shows a clear mistake.
Closed by the strategy after a single bar for a small gain; too little path to judge the late-buy concern or the 4R target. Blind grade stands.

Strategy close after one bar with excursions under 0.1R yet a large positive net; the payoff does not fit the path, likely an accounting artifact. Not evidence about the decision, so the grade stands.
Extended entry still worked: price reached 3.3R, right at the target, before reversing into the stop for a small net gain. A slightly closer target would have been cleanly hit. Blind grade stands.
Counter-trend fade in weak ADX survived a 2R adverse swing and then hit the far target for a big win. Luck of path: the drawdown nearly stopped it out, so the D stands despite the result.
Stale setup with thin edge was stopped out in two bars with a loss over 2R, larger than the stop distance, which suggests slippage or costs. Fading a steady climb was the right thing to flag.
Breakout in a narrow mean-reverting range went nowhere, with a small adverse then small favourable path and a flat close by reconciliation. Break-even result fits the lack of follow-through.
Short breakout never worked: best excursion was 0.07R and price rose to the stop over many bars. The news layer reduce flag and mediocre ADX were warnings, but the stop was sound. Blind C stands.
Weak chop short ended slightly positive via reconciliation after reaching 1.1R, so the wide stop caused no harm here. A modest win from a weak setup does not lift the grade.

An 11R target judged not credible was hit, but only after a 2.5R adverse excursion that a normal stop would not have survived. Pure path luck; the blind D stands and the win should not be learned from.

Fade in chop endured a 5R adverse move before reaching its target for a large gain. The drawdown depth shows how close to ruin it was; outcome is survivorship rather than evidence the setup was sound.
Trend-direction short reached a target judged too far, after a 1.6R adverse swing. The trend context was real, which the blind grade already credited; keep C rather than reward the path.
Low-ADX breakout reached 0.8R then reversed to a full stop loss. Absent trend backing, failure is consistent with the blind concern. Bracket worked as designed.
Entry after the impulse had little room; price barely moved in favour and stopped out slightly over 1R. A fair trade in a trending regime that simply failed; grade stands.
Chop short with a trivial gap and a market still climbing stopped out in eight bars after a 0.5R peak. The skip call at decision time was right.
Retraced pullback with low conviction never went in favour beyond 0.1R and ended near a full stop. Risk was controlled as expected; the weak-edge concern was valid but not enough to drop the grade.
Closed by the strategy after one bar for a small loss with tiny excursions in both directions. Too short to test the thesis; the trend-aligned B grade is untouched.
Chased the breakout bar and was stopped within one bar with no favourable excursion. Maximal confidence did not offset the chase and the chop regime; the D was right.
Stretched short with a very wide stop gave no meaningful favourable move over many bars and lost about one R. Wide stop merely delayed the loss; skip was the better action.
Rebound long never advanced beyond 0.15R and bled to a time exit with a half-R loss. Time exit worked, but a stale idea should have been cut sooner. Blind C still reasonable.
Early fade of a decline absorbed a 2R adverse move and then reached its target for a solid gain. The early entry was costly in drawdown; result is positive but the blind C already reflected the risk.
Selling the extension at very low confidence gained at most 0.6R before reversing through the stop. Low conviction plus an extended price was correctly judged weak.
Strategy close after one bar, loss of 0.7R exceeding the adverse excursion; cost and exit mechanics, not the thesis, drove the result. Decision-time evidence was sound, so B stands.
Countertrend entry below the gap sat for a very long time, saw about 1R in favour, and was closed by reconciliation at a loss. The extra-wide stop let a poor idea linger far too long.
Loss of over 5R from a stop-out with small adverse excursion confirms the bracket was broken, as the blind pass flagged. Inconsistent geometry should have forced a skip; downgrade from C to D.
Tiny gap and a tight stop meant cost and slippage swamped the risk: stopped in one bar for a 2R loss on under 1R adverse movement. The decision-time stop tightness warranted a skip; downgrade to D.
Price reached over 3R, near the target, with almost no adverse move, then returned and exited flat. A somewhat closer target or a trailing stop would have banked it. Blind grade stands.
Drifting entry in chop with heavy correlated exposure fell nearly 3R and lost close to 2R, worse than a clean stop. The wide stop and crowded book made this costly.
A very large win after a 6R adverse excursion, far beyond the reported stop, means the stored stop distance cannot be trusted. Result is not evidence the chop breakout was good; keep D.
Trend breakout with strong conviction reversed quickly and stopped out at about one R after a brief half-R gain. A good decision that lost; no reason to move the grade.
Marked as a stop exit yet net positive despite 1R adverse movement and only 0.26R favourable; the payoff does not fit the path. Wide stop and crowded opposing book still argue against the trade.
Reconciliation closed it after one bar with a large gain unrelated to the excursions. Clean book and decent confidence made the entry fine; the payoff reveals nothing about the decision.
Rangebound entry with no real dip went 1.45R against and was closed by reconciliation at about a full loss. Blind pass noted the absent pullback; the weakness stands but C is kept.
Reached about 1.1R then reversed to a sizeable loss before reconciliation closed it. Low conviction against a heavily opposed book gave little cushion; blind grade stands.
Catching the falling market did bounce 3R after the stop but the tiny stop was hit first, ending near break-even. Wrong-way entry and inconsistent bracket still justify D.
A 15R target was hit after a 2.6R adverse swing, a path few stops would survive. A rare outlier win from a low-confidence entry; do not let it move the grade.
Noise-level stop with the sweep extreme at the entry; the bracket marked take-profit yet net was slightly negative after a large excursion. Reported prices are suspect; skip remains right.
Chop short against rising price still hit its target for a good gain with only a half-R adverse move. A favourable result does not repair the wide stop and crowded book; D stands.
Closed by reconciliation within three bars at a modest loss, with 0.85R adverse and almost no favourable move. Moderate chop breakout; too brief to say more. Grade stands.
Quiet-range breakout failed at once and stopped out near one R. Volatility expansion was possible but did not come; the trade matched its blind assessment.
Strategy close after one bar with a positive payoff exceeding the excursions, an accounting oddity. The lowest-ADX flat-chop entry had no basis, so F stands regardless of the gain.
Chop breakout drifted down and was stopped within two bars after a brief half-R gain. Maximal confidence was unsupported by trend; skip was right.
Stale chop short peaked near 0.6R, then faded to a time exit at a half-R loss. The time exit limited damage but the trade should have been cut or skipped; blind D stands.
Closed after one bar by reconciliation for a small gain; it dipped most of a risk unit first, so the bounce-from-lows doubt held, but the bracket never got to act.
Large win only because the wrong-sided stop never fired despite a drawdown past two risk units; luck of a broken bracket, not skill. The target left roughly half the run on the table.
Target hit cleanly with almost no adverse move, yet the chop regime and stale entry judged at decision time were real flaws; a winning scalp does not repair a 5 ATR stop.
Ran nearly four risk units in favour then reversed all the way through the stop for a loss beyond one unit; the trail was too loose to bank any of it, though the odds were always modest.
Strategy closed it after one bar for a loss near half a unit with little movement either way; the non-premium bounce entry gave no edge, and the blind grade stands.
Stopped in a single bar with slippage beyond one unit in a violent tape; the 0.84 ATR stop was too tight for that volatility, which the blind note flagged only as a small target.
Stopped within three bars after almost no favourable move; a continuation entry far from the midline can fail fast, but the setup quality was sound and one fast loss does not change it.
Won big while sitting more than four units under water, so the wrong-sided stop clearly was not enforced; the unconfirmed reversal in chop was a coin flip rescued by a broken bracket.
Very large win with a shallow drawdown, but the stop on the wrong side of a short means the realised risk was undefined; the result confirms the setup worked, not that the bracket was safe.
Strategy closed after one bar for a trivial gain with almost no excursion either way; chasing a rebound with oversized stop and target produced nothing, so the late-entry critique stands.
Positive close after a long hold but through a drawdown past five units and a peak above ten; the stop sat inside noise and the profit is an artifact of a malformed bracket, so F stands.
Went over twenty units in favour yet closed barely positive after a drawdown near twelve units; the trade was unmanaged noise from a broken stop, and the trivial gap never justified entry.
Eighty-odd bars of drifting without ever reaching the target, then stopped slightly beyond one unit; a late entry in a transitional regime with a wide stop gave no edge to start with.
Faded rally paid eleven units with almost no drawdown, so the idea itself worked, yet the wrong-sided stop meant the claimed risk was fictional; a good result from an unreliable bracket.
Target hit in two bars with tiny adverse move, so the volume spike did continue; but a one-bar event in chop with a wrong-sided stop was still an unsafe basis, and the grade stays.
Never moved in favour and lost about half a unit within eight bars, exactly the false break the range-bound tape suggested; stop and trail were sound, entry was the weakness.
Target hit in three bars despite a drawdown near three units that a valid stop would have taken out; the win depended on the invalid bracket, not on the sharp-slide long being sound.
Large gain over a long hold, closed by reconciliation near the peak; the 0.6 ATR stop survived a drawdown past two units only because it was not enforced as designed, so the flaw stands.
Reported as a stop exit yet booked nearly seven units with under one unit of favourable move, which is inconsistent; the tiny-stop, stale-sweep design cannot be credited with that number.
Slow twenty-bar fade to a roughly one-unit stop with only a small early gain; the stale displacement and sweep noted at decision time were the reason, and the 2.8 ATR stop behaved properly.
Big win through a drawdown near six units; with no gap, low confidence and a wrong-sided stop there was no supportable reason to enter, so the profit is luck and F is kept.
Half a unit in favour over fifty bars before stopping at about one unit loss; fresh sweep, real gap and sane stop were all correct, so this is a normal loser from a decent setup.
Lost nearly eight units after a drawdown beyond thirty-seven over four hundred bars, while a 0.36 ATR stop should have capped it near one; risk was never contained, so the weak setup earns F.
Target hit with only mild drawdown and more room beyond it; the break itself was good, but a 0.9 ATR stop against a 2.5 ATR design was a latent flaw that happened not to bite.
Stopped just under one unit after about half a unit of gain; the wide scalp stop and opposing exposure were fair concerns, and this ordinary loss does not justify moving the grade.
Small win in four bars while the move reached over one and a half units; proportionate stop and gap held up, and a target farther out would have paid more.
Almost no favourable movement in twenty-four bars before a full stop, as expected for a dead tape; the oversized stop and target on a stale sweep had no chance to pay.
Never got going and was stopped slightly past one unit; fighting a steady grind in a strong-ADX tape is why odds were poor, and the sensible stop placement did its job.
Sixteen units won through a drawdown over ten, so the wrong-sided stop was clearly not enforced; the chop-regime gap worked out, but nothing here shows a bracket anyone could rely on.
Thirty bars to a full stop after a brief gain of a third of a unit; chop at low ADX and a wide scalp stop capped the edge as described, and the loss is unremarkable.
Got to nearly a full unit in profit over eighty bars then reversed to the stop; the trend setup was sound, and the wide stop left no cushion once momentum faded.
Stopped in five bars with a modest early gain; the slightly tight 2.0 ATR stop did get hit, but the break from the range bottom with strong ADX was well supported and the grade holds.
No favourable movement at all and a stop-out beyond one unit; the knife-catch against a news reduction advisory played out as flagged, so the blind grade is confirmed.
Reconciliation closed it within a bar for a loss just over half a unit, with a brief gain first; too short to learn anything, and the mid-range no-break read still stands.
Strategy closed after a day for a small loss despite nearly a unit in favour on the way; the low-hit-rate trailed design was cut short before it could deliver its asymmetric payoff.
Sideways drift ended by reconciliation around one unit down, never reaching a third of a unit up; thin structure and weak confidence were the right reading, so no grade change.
Strategy closed for a decent gain with another stretch of favourable room; odds in chop with a crowded book were still weak, so the winning outcome does not lift the grade.
Peaked over twenty-six units up, then lost eighteen with a drawdown past nine; a wrong-sided stop meant no real risk limit existed, and the loss size shows how unsafe this was.
Time exit near flat after peaking at about four fifths of a unit; the small gap and wide stop gave the 1.5R target too far to reach, so a nearer target would have banked something.
Huge win after ninety bars through a drawdown past five units; the stale sweep and wrong-sided stop meant the risk was undefined, so the outcome is not evidence for the setup.
Quick stop within ten bars with a slip past one unit and a small prior gain; entry evidence and proportionate stop were solid, so this is just a normal loss.
Closed by reconciliation after one bar near minus nine tenths despite a modest drawdown, so the loss owes more to the exit mechanics than the path; the news reduce signal was fair warning.
Reconciled flat-to-slightly-negative after five bars with little movement either way; the standard stop and trail design never got tested, so the pullback-in-trend read stays.
Reached the target area and closed with a gain around one and a half units while the move extended to nearly three; the wide stop was barely needed, and the small-gap doubt was too harsh.
Stopped in two bars with slippage past one unit after a gain of three quarters of a unit; the slightly tight 2.0 ATR stop was clipped, supporting the earlier worry about the unconfirmed break.
Chasing a volume-bar rebound in chop gave a third of a unit of gain then a full stop after thirty-four bars; the oversized scalp bracket never had realistic odds, so D holds.
Target hit in thirteen bars despite a drawdown past two units that a valid stop would have cut; entry did follow a gap move, but the win leaned on an unenforced, wrong-sided stop.
Price never moved in favour (best excursion near zero) and ran straight to the very wide stop; the late short under the gap had no edge, so the blind D stands.
Closed by reconciliation after one bar with a small loss and no favourable move; fading a steady advance below the gap was weak, and the outcome adds nothing new.
Big win, but the position swung over 11R against it with a 0.37 ATR stop that never bound, so the win was luck on a fragile bracket; the thesis was still weak. Blind D stands.
Sound sweep-and-displacement short that simply failed to follow through; it barely got half an R of room before the stop beyond the sweep was hit. A good decision that lost.
Winner ran far past the target, but it went more than 1R against the fragile 0.59 ATR stop on the way and survived by luck. The bracket mismatch flagged at decision time was real.

Target hit after a long hold despite a weak range setup and a stop tighter than the structural risk; the logged net exceeds the logged excursion, so the R figures look unreliable. Win does not rescue the grade.
Bounce short in a decline gave almost no favourable excursion before the stop. Crowding was already priced into the blind grade, so no new evidence; keep B.
Squeeze release in a low-ADX chop with thin volume faded after a brief pop; the blind C already doubted the conviction scores, and the stop was taken cleanly.
Range-top fade never reached the distant gap and was stopped, with some slippage past the stop. Reasonable mean-reversion idea with thin volume; the middling grade fits.
Closed by the strategy after one bar for roughly flat; too little path to judge. The trend-pullback logic was sound and the wide stop and long target were never tested.
Strategy closed it after one bar with a modest gain larger than the logged favourable excursion, so the path data is inconsistent. Thin pullback context stays a C.
Target hit after a very long hold, near the best excursion; yet the 0.62 ATR stop was nearly breached and the sweep risk was far larger. A fragile bracket that happened to survive.
Long chased after the bounce ran, with a huge stop; it sat for a long time with almost no favourable move and was closed by reconciliation at about a full loss. Skip.
Breakout reached over 1.3R in favour then gave it all back and was closed by reconciliation near flat; a trail that locked in part of the move would have helped. Marginal setup, C holds.
Range breakout worked despite a very low ADX and faint volume, after going 1.6R against first. The false-breakout risk named in the blind grade was real, so the win is not evidence for an upgrade.
Stale short won, but it went over 2R against a stop that was tighter than the structure, so the stop did not actually hold. Outcome came from luck, not from the setup.
Full loss logged after one bar although the worst excursion was tiny, so the close looks like a reconciliation artifact rather than a trade result. Decision quality unchanged: A.
Hit target after a long hold and the move ran twice as far; the stop inside the sweep distance was not tested badly this time. Setup quality was average, so C stays.
Continuation short closed by reconciliation after one bar with a near-full loss despite a tiny adverse move; that is a bookkeeping exit, not a verdict on the setup. Keep B.
Base breakout closed by reconciliation within two bars for a small loss; no real test of the thesis. Slightly extended entry was already noted in the blind grade.
Marginal breakout over an oscillating range got three-quarters of an R at best, then reversed to the stop after a long hold. Matches the blind concern about a weak, crowded-against setup.
Logged as a target exit yet net negative, so costs or bracket handling ate the gain after a long hold. Low-confidence short with a huge stop remains a skip.
Tiny gain on a one-bar strategy close; stacking another short on an already crowded same-direction book was the problem and the small win does not change it.
Break in a dead-flat tape drifted half an R in favour and reversed into the stop, the whipsaw predicted at decision time. Should have been skipped.
Orderly breakout closed by reconciliation after one bar at roughly a full loss with modest adverse movement; looks like an accounting close, so the decent-breakout grade stands.
Momentum-free breakout in a choppy market, crowded against by the rest of the book, wandered for a while and hit the stop. Nothing here argues for a higher grade.
Late continuation entry closed flat by the strategy after one bar; no meaningful path to evaluate, so the average grade is unchanged.
Fading a strong climb with no trigger never went in favour at all before the stop. A clear skip, as the blind pass said.
Big winner that ran more than twice as far as the target, but the 0.7 ATR stop was almost hit first and the book was already heavily long. Luck on a bad bracket; D stands.
A stop smaller than one tick could not be enforced: the position swung over 11R against it before closing. The huge reported gain is a tiny-denominator artifact. Unbounded risk deserves F.
Counter-trend long against a firm downtrend barely moved in favour and was stopped. The poor reward for the risk was visible beforehand.
A 0.07 ATR stop was blown through by an adverse move of about 30R before the target filled. The enormous logged gain is a denominator artifact; the true risk was uncontrolled. F.
Weak-conviction dip trade reached over 3.5R in favour during a very long hold and was closed slightly negative. The thin premise was visible, and exit management gave the move back.
Stale, far-from-zone entry in chop sat for a long time with only a third of an R in favour before the stop. Skip.
Fade off a range top never went in favour; it drifted for many bars and was stopped. A 1.5R target on a very wide stop is a poor trade structure, but the idea was acceptable.
Mild-dip buy closed by the strategy after one bar with a small loss; too short to judge, and the middling grade for low conviction and a crowded book stays.
A 0.04 ATR stop is untradeable; the trade drew down about 31R before the target filled. The giant gain is arithmetic on a near-zero risk denominator, not skill. F for unbounded risk.
Chop-range short went over 4R in favour but the trailing stop only locked in about 1R after a long hold. A profitable result from a setup that should have been skipped; D stands.
Strong breakout hit its small target quickly with little drawdown, and the move continued past it. The blind view that the target was too close for this much momentum was right.
Short after a sharp unwind with mixed context went half an R in favour, then spiked against the position past its stop. The mixed context the blind grade named is consistent with this.
Clean sweep-and-drop short closed by the strategy after one bar with a decent gain and tiny adverse move. Matches the blind assessment; no reason to upgrade on a single quick win.
Won quickly in only two bars from a stale, tiny-gap setup with a stop inside the structural risk. Fast fill looks like volatility luck rather than a quality entry.
Textbook breakout shape stalled and reversed to the stop; the crowding and modest conviction were already factored in. A reasonable trade that lost, so B stays.
Went almost 4R in favour yet ended near breakeven on the stop, so the exit let a big move vanish. A low-confidence drift setup that should have been skipped regardless.
Sensible decline-bounce short, contrarian to the rest of the book, reached two-thirds of an R then reversed to the stop. Average setup with an ordinary loss.
Chased long won after a long hold, but it went over 3R against a 0.62 ATR stop that should have been hit. The stop did not bind, so this was luck on a mismatched bracket.
Lowest-conviction signal went about half an R in favour, then dropped over 2R against the position before the stop filled. The trade should not have fired.
